title: How to hear this sermon
english: This is a listening version of John Wesley's sermon, Upon Our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse Ten. It is the sermon as printed in John Wesley's 1771 Works. Rendered in modern English.

title: Judge not
english: Judge not, so that you will not be judged. Matthew 7:1.

title: The measure you use
english: For with what judgment you judge, you shall be judged, and with what measure you measure, it shall be measured to you again. Matthew 7:2.

title: The mote and the beam
english: And why do you behold the mote that is in your brother's eye, but do not consider the beam that is in your own eye? Matthew 7:3.

title: Let me pull out the mote
english: Or how will you say to your brother, Let me pull out the mote out of your eye, and behold, a beam is in your own eye? Matthew 7:4.

title: First cast out the beam
english: You hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of your own eye, and then you shall see clearly to cast out the mote out of your brother's eye. Matthew 7:5.

title: Holy things and pearls
english: Do not give that which is holy to dogs, neither cast your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet and turn again and tear you. Matthew 7:6.

title: Ask, seek, knock
english: Ask, and it shall be given to you. Seek, and you shall find. Knock, and it shall be opened to you. Matthew 7:7.

title: Everyone who asks
english: For everyone who asks receives, and he who seeks finds, and to him who knocks, it shall be opened. Matthew 7:8.

title: Bread or a stone
english: Or what man is there among you who, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Matthew 7:9.

title: A fish or a serpent
english: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a serpent? Matthew 7:10.

title: How much more
english: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more shall your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him? Matthew 7:11.

title: The law and the prophets
english: Therefore all things whatever you would have men do to you, do even so to them. For this is the law and the prophets. Matthew 7:12.

title: The hindrances to this religion
english: Our blessed Lord, having now finished his main design, having first delivered the sum of true religion, carefully guarded against those glosses of men by which they would make the word of God of no effect, and having next laid down rules touching that right intention which we are to preserve in all our outward actions, now proceeds to point out the main hindrances to this religion, and concludes all with a suitable application.

title: Inward religion described
english: In the fifth chapter our great Teacher has fully described inward religion in its various branches. He has there laid before us those dispositions of soul which constitute real Christianity: the tempers contained in that holiness without which no man shall see the Lord (Hebrews 12:14); the affections which, when flowing from their proper fountain, from a living faith in God through Christ Jesus, are intrinsically and essentially good and acceptable to God. In the sixth he has shown how all our actions likewise, even those that are indifferent in their own nature, may be made holy and good and acceptable to God by a pure and holy intention. Whatever is done without this, he declares, is of no value with God; whereas whatever outward works are thus consecrated to God are in his sight of great price.

title: Break through all
english: In the former part of this chapter he points out the most common and most fatal hindrances to this holiness. In the latter, he exhorts us by various motives to break through all and secure that prize of our high calling (Philippians 3:14).

title: Judge not others
english: The first hindrance he cautions us against is judging. Judge not, so that you will not be judged. Judge not others, so that you will not be judged by the Lord, so that you will not bring vengeance on your own heads. For with what judgment you judge, you shall be judged, and with what measure you measure, it shall be measured to you again: a plain and equitable rule, by which God permits you to determine for yourselves in what manner he shall deal with you in the judgment of the great day.

title: No station exempt
english: There is no station of life, nor any period of time, from the hour of our first repenting and believing the gospel until we are made perfect in love, in which this caution is not needful for every child of God. For occasions of judging can never be lacking. And the temptations to it are innumerable, many of which are so artfully disguised that we fall into the sin before we suspect any danger. And unspeakable are the mischiefs produced by it: always to him who judges another, thus wounding his own soul and exposing himself to the righteous judgment of God; and frequently to those who are judged, whose hands hang down, who are weakened and hindered in their course, if not wholly turned out of the way and caused to draw back even to perdition (Hebrews 10:39). Yes, how often, when this root of bitterness springs up, are many defiled by it (Hebrews 12:15), by reason of which the way of truth itself is spoken evil of, and that worthy name blasphemed by which we are called.

title: They condemn whom they should imitate
english: Yet it does not appear that our Lord designed this caution only or chiefly for the children of God, but rather for the children of the world, for the men who do not know God. These cannot but hear of those who are not of the world, who follow after the religion described above: who endeavor to be humble, serious, gentle, merciful, and pure in heart; who earnestly desire such measures of these holy tempers as they have not yet attained; and wait for them in doing all good to all men and patiently suffering evil. Whoever goes but this far cannot be hidden, no more than a city set upon a hill (Matthew 5:14). And why do not those who see their good works glorify their Father who is in heaven? What excuse have they for not treading in their steps? For not imitating their example and being followers of them, as they are also of Christ (1 Corinthians 11:1)? Why, in order to provide an excuse for themselves, they condemn those whom they ought to imitate. They spend their time in finding out their neighbor's faults instead of amending their own. They are so busy about others going out of the way that they themselves never come into it at all: at least, never get forward, never go beyond a poor dead form of godliness without the power (2 Timothy 3:5).

title: Cast out the beam first
english: It is to these more especially that our Lord says, Why do you behold the mote that is in your brother's eye: the infirmities, the mistakes, the imprudence, the weakness of the children of God; but do not consider the beam that is in your own eye? You do not consider the damnable impenitence, the satanic pride, the accursed self-will, the idolatrous love of the world which are in yourself, and which make your whole life an abomination to the Lord. Above all, with what supine carelessness and indifference are you dancing over the mouth of hell? And how then, with what grace, with what decency or modesty, will you say to your brother, Let me pull out the mote out of your eye: the excess of zeal for God, the extreme self-denial, the too great disengagement from worldly cares and employments, the desire to be day and night in prayer or hearing the words of eternal life? And behold, a beam is in your own eye! Not a mote, like one of these. You hypocrite! Who pretends to care for others and has no care for your own soul! Who makes a show of zeal for the cause of God, when in truth you neither love nor fear him! First cast out the beam out of your own eye. Cast out the beam of impenitence. Know yourself. See and feel yourself a sinner. Feel that your inward parts are very wickedness, that you are altogether corrupt and abominable, and that the wrath of God abides on you. Cast out the beam of pride. Abhor yourself. Sink down as in dust and ashes. Be more and more little and mean, and base and vile in your own eyes. Cast out the beam of self-will. Learn what that means: If any man will come after me, let him renounce himself (Matthew 16:24). Deny yourself and take up your cross daily. Let your whole soul cry out, I came down from heaven (for so you did, you never-dying spirit, whether you know it or not) not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me (John 6:38). Cast out the beam of love of the world. Love not the world, neither the things of the world (1 John 2:15). Be crucified to the world, and the world crucified to you. Only use the world, but enjoy God. Seek all your happiness in him. Above all, cast out the grand beam, that supine carelessness and indifference. Deeply consider that one thing is needful (Luke 10:42), the one thing which you have scarcely ever thought of. Know and feel that you are a poor, vile, guilty worm, quivering over the great gulf! What are you? A sinner born to die: a leaf driven before the wind: a vapor ready to vanish away: just appearing, and then scattered into air, to be no more seen! See this, and then you shall see clearly to cast out the mote out of your brother's eye. Then, if you have leisure from the concerns of your own soul, you shall know how to correct your brother also.

title: What judging is forbidden
english: But what is properly the meaning of this word, Judge not? What is the judging which is here forbidden? It is not the same as evil speaking, although it is frequently joined with it. Evil speaking is the relating of anything that is evil concerning an absent person; whereas judging may indifferently refer either to the absent or the present. Neither does it necessarily imply speaking at all, but only thinking evil of another. Not that every kind of thinking evil of others is that judging which our Lord condemns. If I see one commit robbery or murder, or hear him blaspheme the name of God, I cannot refrain from thinking ill of the robber or murderer. Yet this is not evil judging: there is no sin in this, nor anything contrary to tender affection.

title: Thinking against love
english: The thinking of another in a manner that is contrary to love is that judging which is here condemned. And this may be of various kinds. For, first, we may think another to blame when he is not. We may lay to his charge (at least in our own mind) the things of which he is not guilty: the words which he has never spoken, or the actions which he has never done. Or we may think his manner of acting was wrong, although in reality it was not. And even where nothing can justly be blamed, either in the thing itself or in the manner of doing it, we may suppose his intention was not good, and so condemn him on that ground, at the same time that he who searches the heart sees his simplicity and godly sincerity.

title: Condemning beyond desert
english: But we may not only fall into the sin of judging by condemning the innocent, but also, secondly, by condemning the guilty in a higher degree than he deserves. This species of judging is likewise an offense against justice as well as mercy, and yet such an offense as nothing can secure us from but the strongest and tenderest affection. Without this, we readily suppose one who is acknowledged to be in fault to be more in fault than he really is. We undervalue whatever good is found in him. No, we are not easily induced to believe that anything good can remain in him in whom we have found anything that is evil.

title: Love thinks no evil
english: All this shows a manifest lack of that love which thinks no evil (1 Corinthians 13:5): which never draws an unjust or unkind conclusion from any premises whatever. Love will not infer, from a person's falling once into an act of open sin, that he is accustomed to do so, that he is habitually guilty of it. And if he was habitually guilty once, love does not conclude he is so still: much less, that if he is now guilty of this, therefore he is guilty of other sins also. These evil reasonings all pertain to that sinful judging which our Lord here guards us against, and which we are in the highest degree concerned to avoid, if we love either God or our own souls.

title: No sentence before proof
english: But supposing we do not condemn the innocent, neither the guilty any farther than they deserve: still we may not be altogether clear of the snare. For there is a third sort of sinful judging, which is the condemning of any person at all where there is not sufficient evidence. And be the facts we suppose ever so true, yet that does not acquit us. For they ought not to have been supposed but proved, and until they were, we ought to have formed no judgment. I say, until they were: for neither are we excused, although the facts admit of ever so strong proof, unless that proof is produced before we pass sentence and compared with the evidence on the other side. Nor can we be excused if ever we pass a full sentence before the accused has spoken for himself. Even a Jew might teach us this, as a mere lesson of justice abstracted from mercy and brotherly love. Does our law, says Nicodemus, judge any man before it hears him and knows what he does (John 7:51)? Yes, a Heathen could reply, when the chief of the Jewish nation desired to have judgment against his prisoner, It is not the manner of the Romans to judge any man before he who is accused has the accusers face to face and has license to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him (Acts 25:16).

title: Second thoughts and counsel
english: Indeed we could not easily fall into sinful judging, were we only to observe that rule which another of those Heathen Romans affirms to have been the measure of his own practice. “I am so far,” says he, “from lightly believing every man's, or any man's, evidence against another, that I do not easily or immediately believe a man's evidence against himself. I always allow him second thoughts, and many times counsel too.” Go, you who are called a Christian, and do likewise, lest the Heathen rise and condemn you in that day (Matthew 12:41).

title: Tell him his fault alone
english: But how rarely should we condemn or judge one another? At least, how soon would that evil be remedied, were we to walk by that clear and express rule which our Lord himself has taught us? If your brother shall trespass against you (or if you hear or believe that he has), go and tell him of his fault between you and him alone (Matthew 18:15). This is the first step you are to take. But if he will not hear, take with you one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established (Matthew 18:16). This is the second step. If he neglects to hear them, tell it to the church: either to the overseers of it or to the whole congregation. You have then done your part. Then think of it no more, but commend the whole to God.

title: Zeal without knowledge
english: But supposing you have, by the grace of God, cast the beam out of your own eye, and do now clearly see the mote or the beam which is in your brother's eye, yet beware that you do not receive hurt yourself by endeavoring to help him. Still do not give that which is holy to dogs. Do not lightly account any to be of this number. But if it evidently appears that they deserve the title, then do not cast your pearls before swine. Beware of that zeal which is not according to knowledge (Romans 10:2). For this is another great hindrance in their way who would be perfect as their heavenly Father is perfect (Matthew 5:48). Those who desire this cannot but desire that all mankind should partake of the common blessing. And when we ourselves first partake of the heavenly gift, the divine evidence of things not seen, we wonder that all mankind do not see the things which we see so plainly, and make no doubt at all but we shall open the eyes of all we have any intercourse with. Hence we are for attacking all we meet without delay and constraining them to see, whether they will or not. And by the ill success of this intemperate zeal, we often suffer in our own souls. To prevent this spending of our strength in vain, our Lord adds this needful caution (needful to all, but more especially to those who are now warm in their first love; Revelation 2:4): Do not give that which is holy to dogs, neither cast your pearls before swine, lest they trample them underfoot and turn again and tear you (Matthew 7:6).

title: The holy thing
english: Do not give that which is holy to dogs. Beware of thinking that any deserve this name until there is full and incontestable proof, such as you can no longer resist. But when it is clearly and indisputably proved that they are unholy and wicked men, not only strangers to but enemies of God, to all righteousness and true holiness: do not give that which is holy, the holy thing, emphatically so called, to these. The holy, the peculiar doctrines of the gospel, such as were hidden from the ages and generations of old and are now made known to us only by the revelation of Jesus Christ and the inspiration of his Holy Spirit (Colossians 1:26), are not to be prostituted to these men, who do not know if there is any Holy Spirit (Acts 19:2). Not indeed that the ambassadors of Christ (2 Corinthians 5:20) can refrain from declaring them in the great congregation, in which some of these may probably be. We must speak, whether men will hear or whether they will forbear (Ezekiel 2:7). But this is not the case with private Christians. They do not bear that awful character, nor are they under any manner of obligation to force these great and glorious truths on those who contradict and blaspheme, who have a rooted enmity against them. No, they ought not to do so, but rather to lead them as they are able to bear. Do not begin a discourse with these upon remission of sins and the gift of the Holy Spirit. But talk with them in their own manner and upon their own principles. With the rational, honorable, unjust epicure, reason of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come (Acts 24:25). This is the most probable way to make Felix tremble. Reserve higher subjects for men of higher attainments.

title: Do not cast your pearls
english: Neither cast your pearls before swine. Be very unwilling to pass this judgment on any man. But if the fact is plain and undeniable, if it is clear beyond all dispute, if the swine do not endeavor to disguise themselves but rather glory in their shame, making no pretense to purity either of heart or life, but working all uncleanness with greediness (Ephesians 4:19): then do not cast your pearls before them. Do not talk to them of the mysteries of the kingdom (Matthew 13:11): of the things which eye has not seen nor ear heard (1 Corinthians 2:9); which consequently, as they have no other inlets of knowledge, no spiritual senses, it cannot enter into their hearts to conceive. Do not tell them of the exceeding great and precious promises which God has given us in the Son of his love (2 Peter 1:4). What conception can they have of being made partakers of the divine nature, who do not even desire to escape the corruption that is in the world through lust (2 Peter 1:4)? Just as much knowledge as swine have of pearls, and as much relish as they have for them, so much relish have they for the deep things of God, so much knowledge of the mysteries of the gospel, who are immersed in the mire of this world, in worldly pleasures, desires, and cares. O do not cast those pearls before these, lest they trample them under their feet, lest they utterly despise what they cannot understand and speak evil of the things which they do not know. No, it is probable this would not be the only inconvenience which would follow. It would not be strange if they were, according to their nature, to turn again and tear you: if they were to return you evil for good, cursing for blessing, and hatred for your goodwill. Such is the enmity of the carnal mind against God and all the things of God (Romans 8:7). Such is the treatment you are to expect from these if you offer them the unpardonable affront of endeavoring to save their souls from death, to pluck them as brands out of the burning (Amos 4:11)!

title: Ask, and it shall be given
english: And yet you need not utterly despair even of these, who for the present turn again and tear you. For if all your arguments and persuasives fail, there is yet another remedy left, and one that is frequently found effectual when no other method avails. This is prayer. Therefore whatever you desire or want, either for others or for your own soul, ask, and it shall be given to you; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you (Matthew 7:7). The neglect of this is a third grand hindrance to holiness. Still we have not, because we ask not (James 4:2). O how meek and gentle, how lowly in heart, how full of love both to God and man might you have been at this day, if you had only asked? If you had continued instant in prayer (Romans 12:12)! Therefore now, at least, ask, and it shall be given to you. Ask, that you may thoroughly experience and perfectly practice the whole of that religion which our Lord has here so beautifully described. It shall then be given to you to be holy as he is holy, both in heart and in all manner of conduct (1 Peter 1:15-16). Seek in the way he has ordained: in searching the scriptures, in hearing his word, in meditating on it, in fasting, in partaking of the supper of the Lord; and surely you shall find. You shall find that pearl of great price (Matthew 13:46), that faith which overcomes the world (1 John 5:4), that peace which the world cannot give (John 14:27), that love which is the earnest of your inheritance (Ephesians 1:14). Knock: continue in prayer and in every other way of the Lord. Do not be weary or faint in your mind. Press on to the mark (Philippians 3:14). Take no denial. Do not let him go until he blesses you (Genesis 32:26). And the door of mercy, of holiness, of heaven shall be opened to you.

title: None need come short
english: It is in compassion to the hardness of our hearts, so unready to believe the goodness of God, that our Lord is pleased to enlarge upon this head, and to repeat and confirm what he has spoken. For everyone, he says, who asks, receives: so that none need come short of the blessing. And he who seeks, even everyone who seeks, finds the love and the image of God; and to him who knocks, to everyone who knocks, the gate of righteousness shall be opened. So that here is no room for any to be discouraged, as though they might ask or seek or knock in vain. Only remember always to pray, to seek, to knock, and not to be faint (Luke 18:1). And then the promise stands sure. It is firm as the pillars of heaven. Yes, more firm; for heaven and earth shall pass away, but his word shall not pass away (Matthew 24:35).

title: Your Father knows how to give
english: To cut off every pretense for unbelief, our blessed Lord, in the following verses, illustrates yet farther what he has said by an appeal to what passes in our own breasts. What man, he says, is there among you who, if his son asks for bread, will he give him a stone? Will even natural affection permit you to refuse the reasonable request of one you love? Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a serpent? Will he give him hurtful instead of profitable things? So that even from what you feel and do yourselves, you may receive the fullest assurance: on the one hand, that no ill effect can possibly attend your asking; and on the other, that it will be attended with that good effect, a full supply of all your wants. For if you, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more shall your Father who is in heaven, who is pure, unmixed, essential goodness, give good things to those who ask him? Or (as he expresses it on another occasion) give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him (Luke 11:13)? In him are included all good things: all wisdom, peace, joy, love; the whole treasures of holiness and happiness; all that God has prepared for those who love him (1 Corinthians 2:9).

title: Be in charity with all
english: But that your prayer may have its full weight with God, see that you are in charity with all men. For otherwise, it is more likely to bring a curse than a blessing on your own head: nor can you expect to receive any blessing from God while you have not charity toward your neighbor. Therefore let this hindrance be removed without delay. Confirm your love toward one another and toward all men. And love them, not in word only, but in deed and in truth (1 John 3:18). Therefore all things whatever you would have men do to you, do even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets (Matthew 7:12).

title: The royal law
english: This is that royal law, that golden rule of mercy as well as justice, which even the Heathen emperor caused to be written over the gate of his palace: a rule which many believe to be naturally engraved on the mind of everyone who comes into the world. And this much is certain, that it commends itself, as soon as heard, to every man's conscience and understanding: insomuch that no man can knowingly offend against it without carrying his condemnation in his own breast.

title: The sum of the prophets
english: This is the law and the prophets. Whatever is written in that law which God of old revealed to mankind, and whatever precepts God has given by his holy prophets, which have been since the world began (Luke 1:70), they are all summed up in these few words, they are all contained in this short direction. And this rightly understood comprises the whole of that religion which our Lord came to establish upon earth.

title: Negative and positive
english: It may be understood either in a positive or negative sense. If understood in a negative sense, the meaning is, “Whatever you would not have men do to you, do not do to them.” Here is a plain rule, always ready at hand, always easy to be applied. In all cases relating to your neighbor, make his case your own. Suppose the circumstances to be changed, and yourself to be just as he is now. And then beware that you indulge no temper or thought, that no word passes out of your lips, that you take no step which you would have condemned in him upon such a change of circumstances. If understood in a direct and positive sense, the plain meaning of it is, “Whatever you could reasonably desire of him, supposing yourself to be in his circumstance, that do, to the uttermost of your power, to every child of man.”

title: Judge your neighbor no more
english: To apply this in one or two obvious instances. It is clear to every man's own conscience: we would not have others judge us, causelessly or lightly think evil of us. Much less would we have any speak evil of us, publish our real faults or infirmities. Apply this to yourself. Do not do to another what you would not have him do to you, and you will never more judge your neighbor, never causelessly or lightly think evil of anyone. Much less will you speak evil: you will never mention even the real fault of an absent person, unless so far as you are convinced it is absolutely needful for the good of other souls.

title: Do to all as you would
english: Again: we would have all men love and esteem us, and behave toward us according to justice, mercy, and truth. And we may reasonably desire that they should do us all the good they can do without injuring themselves: yes, that in outward things (according to the known rule) their superfluities should give way to our conveniences, their conveniences to our necessities, and their necessities to our extremities. Now then let us walk by the same rule: let us do to all as we would have them do to us. Let us love and honor all men. Let justice, mercy, and truth govern all our minds and actions. Let our superfluities give way to our neighbor's conveniences (and who then will have any superfluities left?). Our conveniences to our neighbor's necessities, our necessities to his extremities.

title: Faith is still the root
english: This is pure and genuine morality. This do, and you shall live (Luke 10:28). As many as walk by this rule, peace be to them and mercy: for they are the Israel of God (Galatians 6:16). But then be it observed, none can walk by this rule (nor ever did from the beginning of the world), none can love his neighbor as himself, unless he first loves God. And none can love God unless he believes in Christ, unless he has redemption through his blood, and the Spirit of God bearing witness with his spirit that he is a child of God. Faith therefore is still the root of all, of present as well as future salvation. Still we must say to every sinner, Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you shall be saved (Acts 16:31). You shall be saved now, and you may be saved forever: saved on earth, that you may be saved in heaven. Believe in him, and your faith will work by love (Galatians 5:6). You will love the Lord your God, because he has loved you: you will love your neighbor as yourself. And then it will be your glory and joy to exert and increase this love, not merely by abstaining from what is contrary to it, from every unkind thought, word, and action, but by showing all that kindness to every man which you would have him show to you.
